name: Slovak Bryndzové Halušky
description: Bryndzové halušky, Slovakia's real national dish, depends on real bryndza, a tangy sheep cheese with a sharp, acidic bite no other cheese quite matches - genuinely hard to find in the US, so this version uses the specific substitute Slovak-American home cooks themselves recommend: sheep or regular feta blended smooth with sour cream and butter, not feta alone. Real technique squeezes excess liquid from the grated potato before mixing the dough.
steps_detailed: Squeeze the grated potato well to remove excess liquid.
Mix with the flour, egg, and a pinch of salt into a sticky dough.
Drop small spoonfuls of the dough into a large pot of boiling salted water, and cook 3-4 minutes until they float.
Blend the feta, sour cream, and butter together until smooth - this real combination is what Slovak-American cooks use in place of bryndza.
Drain the dumplings and toss with the cheese mixture while still hot.
Fry the bacon until crisp and scatter over the top, along with its rendered fat.

name: Slovak Strapačky
description: Strapačky, halušky dumplings mixed with sauerkraut and bacon instead of bryndza, is a real regional variation - its name genuinely means 'shaggy', real technique frying the sauerkraut separately first so it develops real depth before combining.
steps_detailed: Squeeze the grated potato well to remove excess liquid.
Mix with the flour, egg, and a pinch of salt into a sticky dough.
Drop small spoonfuls into boiling salted water and cook 3-4 minutes until they float.
Fry the sauerkraut and bacon together, 6-7 minutes, until the sauerkraut develops real depth.
Drain the dumplings and toss with the sauerkraut and bacon.

name: Slovak Kapustnica (Sauerkraut Soup)
description: Kapustnica, a real hearty sauerkraut soup with smoked meat, is a genuine Slovak Christmas staple, real technique simmering long enough for the sauerkraut's tang to mellow and meld with the smoked meat.

Add the bacon, sausage, sauerkraut, and 2 cups water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until the flavors meld and the sauerkraut mellows.

name: Slovak Potato Pancakes (Zemiakové Placky)
description: Zemiakové placky, crispy grated potato pancakes, are a beloved Slovak dish, real technique squeezing excess liquid from the grated potato so they fry crisp.
steps_detailed: Squeeze the grated potato well to remove excess liquid.
Mix with the garlic, flour, and egg.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, flattening slightly, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Slovak Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad, a common Slovak side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, and sugar together, and toss with the cucumber.

name: Slovak Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Slovakia.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Slovak home cooking outside the specific named dishes.

Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
